title: Aspect-Guided Multi-Level Perturbation Analysis of Large Language Models in Automated Peer Review

bias_targets.methodology: Applying an aspect-guided, multi-level perturbation framework that introduces targeted textual manipulations (e.g., exaggerating contributions, omitting methods, inserting typos, altering reviewer tone, and adding false claims) to papers, reviews, and rebuttals, and measuring the resulting unjustified shifts in LLM-generated review scores and meta-review decisions using directional and invariance statistical tests.

Transforming neutral reviews or rebuttals into hostile, sarcastic, or dismissive text to evaluate if the injected negative sentiment systematically skews the LLM's overall scores and final acceptance decisions.

Inserting typographical errors, awkward phrasing, and disorganized structures into papers and rebuttals to test if LLM reviewers inappropriately penalize core scientific dimensions (like soundness or contribution) based on superficial formatting issues.
